verdict.summary: USB composite control-request handler consumes fully host-controlled ctrl fields (wLength, wIndex, wValue, bRequest), but the decisive sinks are guarded: w_length is clamped to USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ for IN requests (and oversized OUT requests are rejected via goto done) before any ep0 buffer write or req->length assignment; every interface index is checked with 'if (!cdev->config || intf >= MAX_CONFIG_INTERFACES)' before indexing; the OS-descriptor path clamps w_length with min_t(u16, w_length, USB_COMP_EP0_OS_DESC_BUFSIZ) before memset. The historical ep0 buffer overflow via large wLength is fixed by the top-of-function clamp. Residual items (os_desc_req NULL check, endpoints bitmap width vs computed endp max 31, fill_ext_prop bounds for interface 0-255, function-driver setup() return values exceeding the buffer) depend on structures, bind-time allocations, or callees not shown and could not be triggered from statements in this code.

assumptions: req->buf (cdev->req) is at least USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ bytes and os_desc_req->buf at least USB_COMP_EP0_OS_DESC_BUFSIZ; the allocation sites are not in the given code, so the clamps are only meaningful under this framework-provided sizing.

struct usb_function's endpoints bitmap is at least 32 bits wide (not shown); the computed maximum index 'endp = ((w_index & 0x80) >> 3) | (w_index & 0x0f)' is 31, so test_bit(endp, f->endpoints) is in range only if the bitmap holds index 31.
cdev->os_desc_req is successfully allocated at bind time before this handler can run (allocation code not shown); no NULL check exists in this function.

Internal callees (get_string, fill_ext_prop, len_ext_prop, count_ext_prop, set_config, config_desc) perform their own bounds handling on the masked, in-domain arguments passed to them (interface is masked to 0-255 via 'w_value & 0xFF').
config->descriptors[0] is non-NULL for an OTG gadget configuration, per bind-time setup not shown; only 'if (!config) goto done' is verifiable here.
limitations: Candidate: NULL dereference of cdev->os_desc_req ('req = cdev->os_desc_req; req->context = cdev;') has no NULL check in this code, but the trigger requires a bind-time allocation failure path not present in the given statements, so it is speculative.

Candidate: test_bit(endp, f->endpoints) with computed max index 31 could read out of bounds if the endpoints bitmap is narrower than 32 bits; the struct definition is not in the given code, so the trigger could not be instantiated.

Candidate: 'req->length = value' at check_value could exceed the ep0 buffer if a function-driver setup()/configuration setup() callback returns a length larger than the buffer; this is a callee-contract issue (function drivers honor the already-clamped ctrl->wLength), not a value this code's own flow produces.

Candidate: the OS-descriptor RECIP_INTERFACE path passes 'interface = w_value & 0xFF' into fill_ext_prop/len_ext_prop; any bounds handling of the ext_prop array occurs inside those not-shown callees, so an OOB there would be a defect in the callee, not at this in-domain call site.

The const-cast write '*temp = cpu_to_le16(USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ)' overwrites the host-supplied ctrl->wLength; this is the intentional upstream mitigation for the ep0 wLength overflow (and its CVE), not a defect.

verdict.summary: jp2_decode reads attacker-controlled JP2 box arrays with loop bounds taken from unrelated counts: bpcs[] is indexed by the codestream component count while the BPCC box's own count is only warned about (line 174); cdef ents[] is indexed by dec->numchans (CMAP/codestream-derived) with no check against the CDEF box's entry count; and for DIRECT CMAP mappings chantocmptlut stores the unchecked channel index (line 272), which is then passed as a component index to jas_image_setcmpttype. All triggers are instantiated by a crafted JP2 file, producing heap out-of-bounds reads (and an unbounded index into a container accessor) with no guard on any path.

evidence.reason: The loop bounds i by dec->numchans (line 233: derived from the CMAP box's numchans or the codestream's component count), but indexes dec->cdef->data.cdef.ents[i], whose allocation length is the CDEF box's own entry count. The check on line 309 bounds the channo field against dec->numchans, not i against the CDEF array length, and it executes after the ents[i] read. Trigger: CDEF box with 1 entry plus a codestream with N>1 components (no CMAP) gives numchans=N and reads ents[1..N-1] out of bounds; no statement anywhere rejects this.

bpcs[i] is indexed up to the codestream's component count, but bpcs holds only bpcc.numcmpts entries (the BPCC box's own count). The mismatch check at lines 172-175 only prints 'warning: number of components mismatch' and falls through instead of goto error. Trigger: BPCC with numcmpts=1, codestream with 4 mixed-dtype components (samedtype false) reads bpcs[1..3] out of bounds; no rejection or corrected loop bound exists on any path.

Origin of the faulty value: this is the only statement comparing the BPCC entry count to the codestream component count, and it is fail-open — a warning with no goto error — so the mismatched counts propagate to the bpcs[i] sink at line 182.

evidence.snippet:
if (cmapent->map == JP2_CMAP_DIRECT) {
				dec->chantocmptlut[channo] = channo;
evidence.reason: Origin of an unbounded component index: the CMAP sanity loop (lines 240-244) validates the cmptno FIELD, but for DIRECT mappings the code stores the channel index channo (bounded only by the CMAP's attacker-controlled numchans, line 269) into the channel-to-component LUT, discarding the checked cmptno. These values reach jas_image_setcmpttype(dec->image, dec->chantocmptlut[i], ...) at lines 313-317/321-322 with no bound against jas_image_numcmpts(dec->image) on any path; with numchans=256 direct channels and a 1-component image, indices up to 255 are passed into the component-array accessor.

Sink: the component index comes from dec->chantocmptlut[i], which for DIRECT CMAP entries (line 272) holds the raw channel index, bounded only by the attacker-controlled CMAP numchans and never checked against the image's component count; a container accessor is handed an out-of-domain index (e.g. 255 with 1 component), with no validating statement on any path in this code.

assumptions: The box parsers behind jp2_box_get (not shown) allocate bpcs[] with bpcc.numcmpts entries, cdef ents[] with the CDEF box's own entry count, cmap ents[] with cmap.numchans entries, and pclr lutdata with numlutents*numchans entries; without these lengths the OOB claims could not be framed, but they are the standard allocation contract of the box fields this code reads.
jas_image_* accessors are container accessors that index the image's component array; their exact internal bounds behavior is not shown.
JP2_BPCTODTYPE, jp2_getcs, jp2_getct, fromiccpcs semantics assumed per jasper conventions.
limitations: Unchecked jas_alloc2 result for lutents (line 274): a NULL dereference write at line 276 requires allocator failure; a PCLR box with a numlutents large enough to fail would already have required proportional lutdata allocation in the unseen box parser, so the trigger is not instantiated by this code — robustness issue only.

Potential integer overflow in cmapent->pcol + i * pclrd->numchans (line 276) requires numlutents*numchans near 2^32 with an inconsistently small lutdata allocation performed by code not shown; trigger not instantiated here.
cdefd = &dec->cdef->data.cdef (line 268) is computed when dec->cdef may be NULL, but it is an address-of with no dereference and cdefd is consumed only under '#if 0' — no memory access occurs.
assert(dec->image->cmprof_) (line 212) firing or a NULL cmprof_ under NDEBUG depends on jas_cmprof_createfromiccprof (callee not shown); trigger not instantiated by any statement in this code.

jas_iccprof_createfrombuf and jas_image_depalettize receive in-domain arguments under the guards analyzed (icc buffer+len pair; cmptno checked at line 240, pcol checked at line 246, lutents sized from the same numlutents expression as the fill loop); their internal handling is outside this code.

verdict.summary: Cineon (CIN) header decoder. All attacker-derived fields (image_offset, user_length, pixels_per_line, lines_per_image, bits_per_pixel, number_channels) are either bounds-checked against the blob size before use ('if (((MagickSizeType) image->columns*image->rows/8) > GetBlobSize(image)) ThrowReaderException', 'if (cin.file.user_length > GetBlobSize(image)) ThrowReaderException') or used only through fully-enumerated switches, fixed-size struct reads into a zeroed struct, and checked pixel-cache calls (SetImageExtent/QueueAuthenticPixels with NULL checks). The pixel-row copy 'stream=ReadBlobStream(image,length,pixels,&count); if ((size_t) count != length) break;' uses length derived from the same image geometry, but the size of the GetQuantumPixels buffer is set inside AcquireQuantumInfo, which is not part of the given code, so a potential length-vs-buffer mismatch cannot be instantiated here.

assumptions: AcquireQuantumInfo(image_info,image)/GetQuantumPixels(quantum_info) allocate an internal pixel buffer; its size is not shown, so whether GetBytesPerRow(image->columns,3,image->depth,MagickTrue) (the RGB 'length' passed to ReadBlobStream) always fits that buffer cannot be determined from the given code. No guard on this relation exists in the shown code.

GetBytesPerRow and ImportQuantumPixels semantics (internal functions not shown) are assumed to behave as in upstream ImageMagick; in particular depth=0 behavior was not characterizable from the given code.
ReadBlob on truncated files returns fewer bytes; struct fields were zeroed via 'memset(&cin,0,sizeof(cin))' so no uninitialized data reaches the property setters.
limitations: Candidate heap-overflow at 'stream=ReadBlobStream(image,length,pixels,&count)' with 3-channel length vs. the internally allocated quantum buffer could not be instantiated: the allocation site is inside AcquireQuantumInfo, which is not part of the given code, so neither the overflow nor its absence can be proven here.

If bits_per_pixel is 0 (image->depth=0), length computes to 0, the row loop performs empty reads and ImportQuantumPixels with a zero-length stream; no memory-safety consequence was provable from the given code, recorded as a robustness observation only.

image->columns/rows are attacker 32-bit values; the guard ((MagickSizeType) image->columns*image->rows/8) > GetBlobSize(image) bounds raster area to roughly 8x the file size, so no unbounded resource consumption (cache allocation <= ~32x file size) was found.

verdict.summary: In the DEFI chunk handler of ReadOneMNGImage, object_id is derived from attacker chunk bytes ((p[0] << 8) | p[1], up to 65535) and the only bound, 'if (object_id > MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)', uses '>' instead of '>=' and clamps offending ids to MNG_MAX_OBJECTS — an index the code's own CLIP/MOVE handlers ('if ((i < 0) || (i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)) continue;') treat as out of domain. object_id == MNG_MAX_OBJECTS therefore reaches 'if (mng_info->exists[object_id])' (out-of-bounds read) and 'mng_info->exists[object_id]=MagickTrue;' plus 'mng_info->invisible[object_id]=p[2];', 'mng_info->x_off[object_id]=...', 'mng_info->y_off[object_id]=...' (out-of-bounds writes of attacker-chosen 32-bit values) in the MngInfo structure, corrupting heap memory of the process parsing the file.

evidence.reason: Root cause: off-by-one index validation. The guard 'if (object_id > MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)' permits object_id == MNG_MAX_OBJECTS (and its clamp arm assigns exactly MNG_MAX_OBJECTS), while the code's own CLIP/MOVE handlers prove indices >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS are invalid for these arrays. Instantiated trigger: an MNG file containing a DEFI chunk with length >= 2 and id bytes 01 00 (or FF FF, which is clamped to the same value) makes 'if (mng_info->exists[object_id])' read and 'mng_info->exists[object_id]=MagickTrue;' (and, with length > 2 / > 11, 'mng_info->invisible[object_id]=p[2];' and 'mng_info->x_off[object_id]=(ssize_t)((p[4] << 24) | ...)' / y_off) write one element past the end of the exists/frozen/invisible/x_off/y_off arrays in the heap-allocated MngInfo structure — attacker-driven out-of-bounds write (memory corruption) during image parsing.

evidence.snippet: object_id=(p[0] << 8) | p[1];
evidence.reason: Origin of the tainted index: object_id is composed from the first two bytes of the attacker-supplied DEFI chunk payload (p = chunk, filled from the file), yielding any value 0..65535 with no bounds applied at this point; combined with the '>' (instead of '>=') bound and the clamp to MNG_MAX_OBJECTS downstream, values >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS reach the out-of-bounds array accesses.

assumptions: The MngInfo arrays exists[], frozen[], invisible[], x_off[], y_off[], object_clip[] have capacity MNG_MAX_OBJECTS; this is implied by the code's own loops ('for (i=0; i < MNG_MAX_OBJECTS; i++)', 'for (i=1; i < MNG_MAX_OBJECTS; i++)') and the quoted CLIP/MOVE guards 'if ((i < 0) || (i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)) continue;', since the struct declaration is not part of the given code.
MNG_MAX_OBJECTS < 65536, implied by the existence and purpose of the 'object id too large' check applied to a 16-bit value.
limitations: Chunk underfill / uninitialized memory (CWE-908): the only size guard 'if (length > GetBlobSize(image))' compares against the TOTAL blob size, not remaining bytes, and the fill loop exits at EOF ('if (c == EOF) break;') with no check that 'length' bytes were actually read; a chunk declared longer than the remaining file therefore leaves AcquireQuantumMemory (non-zeroing) heap bytes that are consumed as widths, offsets, and palette entries. Impact chain runs into consumers not shown, so not promoted.

tRNS handler: the copy is bounded by 'if (length > 0 && length < 257)' but 'mng_info->global_trns_length=(unsigned int) length;' is outside that guard and can store up to PNG_UINT_31_MAX for a 256-entry array; the harmful indexing occurs in ReadOnePNGImage, which is not shown, so the impact chain is not instantiated here.

MAGN magnification: for a 1-row image with magn_methy > 1, computed magnified_height is 1 but the row loop runs m = magn_mt iterations (branch 'if (y == 0) m=(ssize_t) mng_info->magn_mt;'), so 'yy' can exceed large_image->rows when entry is triggered via width magnification; the only guard is 'assert(yy < (ssize_t) large_image->rows);', which is typically compiled out, and the actual out-of-range behavior depends on the unshown GetAuthenticPixels bounds handling — speculative.
LOOP/ENDL index loop_active[loop_jump/loop_count] with loop_level = chunk[0] (0..255); array declarations are not shown, so out-of-bounds cannot be proven.

DISC handler passes raw attacker ids (up to 65535) to MngInfoDiscardObject, an internal callee not shown; no validation on any path in this code, but the harmful use cannot be located in the given code.
'if (memcmp(type,mng_MEND,4) == 0) break;' exits the loop without freeing the allocated 'chunk' — a bounded single-allocation leak per file, no security effect.

verdict.summary: In ReadOneMNGImage, the CLIP chunk handler indexes MngInfo per-object arrays with attacker-controlled, unvalidated indices. first_object and last_object are read from chunk bytes ((p[0]<<8)|p[1], (p[2]<<8)|p[3], up to 65535) and the loop 'for (i=(int) first_object; i <= (int) last_object; i++)' accesses mng_info->exists[i], frozen[i], and object_clip[i] with no bounds check anywhere on the path (the parallel MOVE handler contains the guard 'if ((i < 0) || (i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)) continue;', proving the required domain). A crafted CLIP chunk with last_object=0xFFFF causes heap out-of-bounds reads and, where the OOB exists[i] word is nonzero, an out-of-bounds write mng_info->object_clip[i]=mng_read_box(box,(char) p[0],&p[1]) of a 32-byte struct with attacker-influenced contents — memory corruption. A secondary off-by-one exists in the DEFI handler: 'if (object_id > MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)' (should be >=) and the clamp 'object_id=MNG_MAX_OBJECTS' permit a one-past write at mng_info->exists[object_id].

evidence.reason: Root cause: first_object/last_object are taken directly from CLIP chunk bytes (0-65535) and used as array indices into mng_info->exists[], frozen[], and object_clip[] with no bound against MNG_MAX_OBJECTS; the only guards on this path ('if (length > 3)' and 'if ((p-chunk) < (ssize_t) (length-17))') bound the chunk-data reads, not the index. Trigger: an MNG file whose CLIP chunk (length 100) carries first_object=0, last_object=0xFFFF; the loop walks i to 65535, reading exists[i]/frozen[i] out of bounds and, where the OOB exists[i] word is nonzero (later MngInfo members such as x_off[] hold nonzero values), performing the out-of-bounds write 'mng_info->object_clip[i]=mng_read_box(box,(char) p[0],&p[1]);' (lines 819-820) with attacker-influenced contents — heap out-of-bounds read and write. The identical MOVE pattern contains the guard 'if ((i < 0) || (i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)) continue;', proving both the required bound and its absence here.

Off-by-one: the comparison uses '>' instead of '>=', and the clamp sets object_id to exactly MNG_MAX_OBJECTS — an index the code's own MOVE handler rejects ('if ((i < 0) || (i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)) continue;'), proving the valid domain is 0..MNG_MAX_OBJECTS-1. Trigger: DEFI chunk with object_id=0xFFFF (or exactly MNG_MAX_OBJECTS) flows to 'mng_info->exists[object_id]=MagickTrue;' (line 406), a one-past write, and subsequent x_off/y_off/object_clip/invisible accesses at the same index. Secondary to the CLIP defect; rests partly on the array size being MNG_MAX_OBJECTS, which is inferred from the code's own loops and MOVE guard.

assumptions: The MngInfo arrays exists[], frozen[], invisible[], viewable[], x_off[], y_off[], object_clip[] are sized MNG_MAX_OBJECTS; the struct declaration is not shown — the domain is inferred from the code's own loops ('for (i=1; i < MNG_MAX_OBJECTS; i++)') and MOVE's guard 'if ((i < 0) || (i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)) continue;'.

mng_get_long, mng_read_box, mng_read_pair, mng_minimum_box, MngInfoDiscardObject, ReadOnePNGImage, and GetAuthenticPixels semantics are not shown; standard/documented semantics were assumed only where characterizable (memory copy, blob read).
The numeric value of MNG_MAX_OBJECTS is not shown; the CLIP finding holds for any plausible value since the index reaches 65535.
limitations: TERM chunk reads mng_get_long(&p[2]) and mng_get_long(&p[6]) guarded only by 'if (length != 0)' for p[0]; with length < 10 this reads uninitialized bytes past the chunk data — but within the length+MagickPathExtent allocation (uninitialized read, not an overflow).
DISC handler passes unvalidated indices i=p[j-1]<<8|p[j] (up to 65535) to MngInfoDiscardObject, whose bounds checking is not shown; impact chain unverifiable in this code.
LOOP/ENDL use loop_level=chunk[0] (0-255) to index loop_active/loop_count/loop_jump/loop_iteration; the MNG_MAX_LOOPS array size is not shown, so OOB cannot be proven from this code alone.

MAGN: magnified_width/height arithmetic ((image->columns-2)*magn_mx, png_uint_32) can overflow, at worst causing the assert(yy < large_image->rows) or a bounds-checked pixel accessor failure — DoS, not instantiated corruption.
LOOP chunk iteration counts up to 2^31-1 with SeekBlob-based rewind enable repeated re-parsing of a tiny file (bounded amplification/DoS).

FRAM's frame-name walk ('while (*p && ((p-chunk) < (ssize_t) length)) p++;') can advance p past the chunk data; subsequent reads stay within the length+MagickPathExtent allocation (uninitialized reads only).

verdict.summary: hfsplus_block_allocate never checks the return value of read_mapping_page (3 call sites) before passing it to kmap and dereferencing it. The page index is derived from attacker-controlled on-disk values (size=total_blocks, offset) and, on a crafted filesystem image whose allocation file does not validly cover the requested page, read_mapping_page returns an ERR_PTR sentinel which is kmap'd and dereferenced in the kernel, causing a wild-pointer dereference/write (kernel oops or memory corruption) when the image is mounted.

evidence.snippet:
page = read_mapping_page(mapping, offset / PAGE_CACHE_BITS, NULL);
	pptr = kmap(page);
evidence.reason: Root cause: the failure sentinel of read_mapping_page (whose page index offset/PAGE_CACHE_BITS is attacker-derived from the filesystem image) is passed directly to kmap with no IS_ERR/NULL check on any path; the first dereference val = *curr (line 28) then operates on a wild pointer. Trigger: attacker mounts an image whose allocation file does not cover the requested page, making read_mapping_page return ERR_PTR.

Scan-loop reload path: the guard at line 55 (if (offset >= size) break;) bounds the page index only by attacker-controlled size, not by the allocation file's actual coverage; an undersized allocation file (page 0 full of set bits forces the reload) yields an error page that is kmap'd and dereferenced at line 42 without any check.

Write-loop reload site with the same unchecked sentinel; here the garbage pptr also feeds *curr = cpu_to_be32(n); at line 120 (done:), giving a wild-write primitive through the unchecked page pointer.

assumptions: read_mapping_page returns a valid page or an ERR_PTR sentinel (standard kernel semantics); its failure for a page the attacker-crafted allocation file does not validly cover (HFS+ is non-sparse; extent entries pointing outside the device yield EIO) is assumed reachable because the allocation file's on-disk layout is attacker data — the not-shown hfsplus readpage implementation cannot be quoted.

size (total_blocks), offset, and *max are passed by callers from state derived from the attacker-supplied volume; no mount-time relation between the allocation file size and total_blocks is shown and none may be relied on.
limitations: Line 124: HFSPLUS_SB(sb).free_blocks -= *max can underflow when the volume header supplies free_blocks < *max; impact depends on free_blocks consumers not shown, so not instantiated as a vulnerability.
Line 54: offset += PAGE_CACHE_BITS is u32 and can wrap near 2^32 blocks, potentially re-scanning pages; triggering requires a near-2^32-block bitmap that is genuinely full of set bits — speculative.

Lines 28/42 can read bitmap words beyond the truncated end within the mapped page (logical over-read past size); the access stays inside the mapped page and any found bit is rejected by if (start >= size) at line 71, so it is memory-safe.

verdict.summary: No reachable vulnerability was instantiated. All memory-index sinks over lines_ga are guarded by quoted bounds checks (`current_line < lines_ga.ga_len`, `lines_ga.ga_len > 0`, `cstack.cs_idx >= 0` combined with `cstack.cs_line[cstack.cs_idx] >= 0` and WHILE/FOR/ACTIVE flag checks), the cmdline_copy/lines_ga ownership lifecycle is kept disjoint by the `cmdline_copy == NULL` -> vim_strsave (NULL-checked) path so no UAF/double-free is producible, and recursion is capped by `call_depth >= 200 && call_depth >= p_mfd`. The remaining OOB/UAF candidates all require internal callees (do_one_cmd, store_loop_line, rewind_conditionals) violating invariants that this code's own statements maintain, so their triggers are not instantiable here.

assumptions: do_one_cmd() (not shown) returns NULL or a pointer into the cmdline_copy buffer past a '|' as its comment states, and maintains cstack.cs_idx/cs_lflags/looplevel consistently with the WHILE/FOR/TRY entries it executes; the `cstack.cs_idx >= 0` guard for the CSL_HAD_FINA block (which indexes cs_pending[cs_idx] without an explicit check) depends on do_one_cmd never setting CSL_HAD_FINA without an active :try.

store_loop_line() appends exactly one wcmd_T entry (a copy of next_cmdline) per successful call, making `cstack.cs_line[cstack.cs_idx] = current_line_before` equal to lines_ga.ga_len-1; this is the structural upper bound protecting the jump-back index at `((wcmd_T *)lines_ga.ga_data)[current_line].lnum-1`, which has no explicit `current_line < lines_ga.ga_len` check in this code.
rewind_conditionals()/cleanup_conditionals() (not shown) keep cs_idx and cs_looplevel in sync and guarantee termination of the trailing `do {...} while (cstack.cs_idx >= 0)` cleanup loop.
fgetline (getexline/getsourceline/get_func_line) returns an allocated, NUL-terminated line owned by this caller; STRMOVE(cmdline_copy, next_cmdline) copies a suffix within the same buffer.
limitations: Stack-exhaustion denial of service: a sourced script can `:set maxfuncdepth=1000000` and then recurse via :source/:call; the guard `call_depth >= 200 && call_depth >= p_mfd` then permits ~maxfuncdepth nested do_cmdline frames (each with a large cstack_T on the stack). This requires the operator-configurable option to be raised and yields only a same-privilege crash of the process the script's own author targets, so it is not promoted to a vulnerability.

Speculative OOB read at `((wcmd_T *)lines_ga.ga_data)[current_line].lnum-1` (breakpoint recheck after :continue/:endwhile jump-back) if any internal callee ever left a WHILE/FOR entry's cs_line >= lines_ga.ga_len or shrank ga_len while looplevel > 0; no statement in this code produces that state, so the trigger is not instantiated.

Speculative heap overflow via STRMOVE(cmdline_copy, next_cmdline) if do_one_cmd() ever returned a pointer outside cmdline_copy; the only in-code contract is the comment `do_one_cmd() will return NULL if there is no trailing '|'`.
Speculative hang in the post-loop `do { ... rewind_conditionals(...) } while (cstack.cs_idx >= 0);` if rewind_conditionals() failed to decrement cs_idx; termination depends on that callee.

verdict.summary: All GRE-header, key, and protocol reads are bounded in execution order by the two pskb_may_pull checks (lines 12 and 25), which validate offset+grehlen after grehlen is grown from attacker-controlled flags and before the re-read at lines 28-29; the key read is exactly at the pull bound and in bounds. The only in-code-unbounded uses - &skb->data[teli] and the ipv6h->daddr/saddr reads - require trigger values (out-of-range callee return, or offset < sizeof(struct ipv6hdr)) that are produced only by code not shown, so no trigger is instantiated in this code.

assumptions: offset is assumed non-negative and at least sizeof(struct ipv6hdr) when it reaches this handler; no statement in this code enforces or documents that precondition (it is computed by the ICMPv6 dispatch layer, not shown).

ip6_tnl_parse_tlv_enc_lim (line 53) is assumed to return either 0 or an offset into linearly-pulled skb data; its implementation is not shown, and its failure sentinel 0 is the only in-code check (`teli && ...`, line 55).
pskb_may_pull(skb, len) is relied on per its documented semantics: on success, bytes skb->data[0..len-1] are linearly accessible; on failure it returns false without modifying accessibility.
limitations: Speculative: OOB read candidate at `tel = (struct ipv6_tlv_tnl_enc_lim *) &skb->data[teli]; if (tel->encap_limit == 0)` (lines 56-57). teli is not bounded against skb length anywhere in this code (line 55 only checks teli != 0 and teli == be32_to_cpu(info)-2), but an out-of-range teli can only be produced by the unshown callee ip6_tnl_parse_tvl_enc_lim returning an unvalidated offset. The historical kernel bug of exactly this shape was fixed inside that callee, not in this function; trigger not instantiable from the given code.

verdict.summary: njs_object_iterate_reverse consumes the int64_t iteration bounds args->from/args->to without any validation. Instantiated trigger: from=4, to=0, value="ab" (size 2) reads S[4] and S[3].

For from = -1 (e.g., args->from = -1, args->to = -1, empty fast array), `-1 < array->length` is true, so njs_is_valid(&array->start[-1]) reads 16 bytes before the allocation and, if the garbage looks like a valid njs_value_t, handler receives an out-of-bounds pointer (type confusion on OOB memory). In the UTF-8 branch the loop runs from+1-to iterations while njs_utf8_prev only walks within the buffer as long as the index range is in bounds; nothing checks from < length or to >= 0, so pos moves before string_prop.start and njs_string_new copies out-of-bounds bytes into a JS string. Origin of the tainted values: from and to are int64_t indices taken verbatim from the args parameter of this non-static function with no documented or enforced range contract anywhere in the code; they flow directly into the pointer-arithmetic sinks at lines 80, 103, and 27.

assumptions: njs_array_t fast_array invariant: array->length does not exceed the allocated size of array->start (internal to njs, not quotable here); the quoted upper-bound guard at line 27 is sound relative to the allocation only under this invariant.

Integer overflow of `from += 1` / `i = from + 1` / `from - to` requires from near INT64_MAX; no path in this code produces such values, and upstream length handling would have to supply them — speculative.

The bottom object-handler loop (lines 164-166) can iterate from-to times with no cap; a caller-supplied huge range would be unbounded consumption (CWE-400), but no in-code producer of such a range is quotable — it shares the same unvalidated-parameter root cause and is not counted separately.

If, in the real product, every caller of this exported helper computes from/to strictly as [0, length-1]/[0], the OOB triggers would not fire from script-observable input; that contract cannot be quoted from the given code, so it was not allowed to dismiss the candidates (per the guard-anchoring rule).

Corrupt input after a CLEAR code can produce garbage output bytes (stale oldcode chain), but all indices stay within the table bounds and no security impact beyond incorrect output was instantiated.
The #ifdef DEBUG block reads p[-1]..p[3] around posbits without bounds checks; it is compiled out on the analyzed path and only reachable in debug builds of corrupt-input handling.

verdict.summary: The GLOB_BRACE expansion loop recurses into glob() once per brace alternative with GLOB_APPEND and leaves GLOB_BRACE set in the recursive flags, so an attacker-supplied pattern of n comma-alternative groups (e.g. "{.,.}" repeated 30 times, ~150 bytes) forces at least 2^n recursive glob() invocations and up to 2^n accumulated, strdup-allocated pglob entries. No statement anywhere in the code bounds the number of recursive invocations, the accumulated entry count, or the recursion depth; the only size check, `newcount > SIZE_MAX / sizeof (char *) - 2`, bounds at ~2^61 entries and provides no DoS protection, and each recursive call restarts `alloca_used = 0` so glob_use_alloca caps nothing cumulatively. This yields attacker-scalable CPU and memory exhaustion in any process that passes an untrusted pattern with GLOB_BRACE.

evidence.reason: Unbounded recursive sink: inside the `while (1)` loop (line 139), each brace alternative triggers a recursive glob() call whose flags preserve GLOB_BRACE (only GLOB_NOCHECK|GLOB_NOMAGIC are cleared and GLOB_APPEND is added), so every level re-enters brace expansion. Trigger fully instantiated: pattern "{.,.}"x30 with GLOB_BRACE produces 2^30 recursive glob() calls (line 144 builds each child pattern; lines 167-169 `p = next + 1; next = next_brace_sub (p, flags); assert (next != NULL);` spawn the second and subsequent alternatives), each leaf performing a directory scan and appending one strdup-allocated entry via ++pglob->gl_pathc. No cap on invocation count, entry count, or recursion depth exists anywhere in the code; the only bound is the SIZE_MAX-scale check `newcount > SIZE_MAX / sizeof (char *) - 2`.

evidence.snippet: if (flags & GLOB_BRACE)
evidence.reason: Origin of the trigger: the attacker-data `pattern` parameter (line 1) of this exported API, combined with the attacker-choosable GLOB_BRACE flag validated as legal by line 16's `(flags & ~__GLOB_FLAGS) != 0` check, enters the exponential brace-expansion machinery here with no accompanying limit on pattern size, expansion factor, or recursion depth.

assumptions: Semantics of the not-shown internal helpers next_brace_sub, glob_use_alloca, alloca_account, glob_in_dir, prefix_array, is_dir, collated_compare, __glob_pattern_type, and scratch_buffer_* are taken as standard glibc (next_brace_sub returns the pointer to the ',' or '}' terminating a brace alternative; glob_in_dir with GLOB_APPEND appends entries and increments gl_pathc). The exponential-trigger claim also rests on the quoted loop structure (lines 139-169), which iterates at least twice per comma-alternative group.
__GLOB_FLAGS includes GLOB_BRACE, so line 16's flag-validation does not reject the trigger input.

The trust-boundary model treats `pattern` as attacker-data per discipline 4 (data-carrying parameter of an exported function); whether a given application passes untrusted patterns with GLOB_BRACE is a deployment fact outside this code and only affects the population of reachable callers, not the defect.
limitations: Memory-safety candidates were examined and dismissed with quoted exact-fit bounds, not on caller/callee responsibility: the brace working buffer onealt of pattern_len = strlen(pattern)-1 bytes is provably sufficient because total copies (begin-pattern) + (next-p) + rest_len never exceed strlen(pattern)-1 (all `next` values point at a ','/'}' at or before the closing brace); the GLOB_TILDE user-name unescape writes at most exactly end_name - dirname bytes (the fixed form `if (filename == NULL) *p++ = '\\';` is present); the home-dir concatenation copies exactly home_len + dirlen bytes into a home_len + dirlen buffer; the GLOB_MARK realloc(len) + strcpy(&new[len-2], "/") fits exactly; the realloc and gl_offs sites are guarded by `newcount > SIZE_MAX / sizeof (char *) - 2` and `pglob->gl_offs >= ~((size_t) 0) / sizeof (char *)`.

NULL-dereference candidates dismissed as provably unreachable: dirname is non-NULL on every path reaching `__glob_pattern_type` (pattern, ".", "/", malloc-checked newp, or tilde-expanded non-NULL home_dir), and the GLOBPAT_BACKSLASH unescape starts from `strchr (dirname, '\\')` only when the meta bit indicates a backslash is present.

assert (next != NULL) at line 169 compiles out under NDEBUG, but the chain invariant (every next_brace_sub result in the main loop re-walks the already-verified path to the closing brace) makes it unreachable-in-domain; not counted as a finding.

Deep nested-brace recursion ({a,{a,...}}) causing stack exhaustion is folded into the CWE-400 finding rather than reported separately; gnulib's GLOB_LIMIT extension demonstrates the recognized fix form that is absent here.

If the evaluation intends this verbatim glibc glob.c to be judged only for memory-safety defects, the verdict would be not-vulnerable; the reported finding is an availability (resource-consumption) defect whose severity depends on callers passing untrusted patterns with GLOB_BRACE.

verdict.summary: In ReadTileMethod, the tile buffer size 'extent=4*(samples_per_pixel+1)*MagickMax(rows*TIFFTileRowSize(tiff),TIFFTileSize(tiff))' is computed from attacker-controlled uint32 TIFF tile dimensions (TILEWIDTH/TILELENGTH) and can wrap size_t to a small value; the resulting undersized heap buffer is then filled by TIFFReadTile with attacker-controlled tile data of independently chosen length, giving a heap out-of-bounds write. The only nearby guard, HeapOverflowSanityCheck(rows,sizeof(*tile_pixels)), checks rows*1 and does not bound the extent product, and the scanline/1.5*number_pixels checks constrain only the unrelated pixel_info buffer.

evidence.reason: Integer overflow in the allocation-size computation: with attacker-chosen tile width/length (uint32, e.g. R*C ~ 2^60 with samples_per_pixel=32, bits_per_sample=1, image 16x16 so all earlier pixel_info gates pass), 4*(samples_per_pixel+1)*rows*TIFFTileRowSize(tiff) wraps mod 2^64 to a small extent, so tile_pixels is allocated far smaller than the TIFF tile size that TIFFReadTile subsequently decodes into it — attacker-controlled heap out-of-bounds write. HeapOverflowSanityCheck validates only rows*sizeof(*tile_pixels)=rows*1, not the extent product.

Origin of the tainted values: tile columns and rows are read directly from attacker-controlled TIFF tags with no range validation (AcquireMagickResource is policy-dependent and quotes no numeric bound), and they feed the overflowing extent computation.

assumptions: AcquireQuantumMemory performs only a count*quantum overflow check; with a wrapped-small nonzero extent it returns a valid small allocation (a 0 extent result is treated as a variant of the same trigger).

Default resource policy (AcquireMagickResource WidthResource/HeightResource) does not cap tile dimensions on unconfigured systems; on installations with a policy.xml width/height limit the trigger requires dimensions under that limit.

libtiff characterizable semantics: TIFFTileRowSize/TIFFTileSize compute tilewidth*spp*bps/8 and rows*tile-row-size in 64-bit, and TIFFReadTile decodes/copies attacker-supplied tile data (bounded by the tile byte counts in the file) into the caller's buffer.
Exact line numbers were counted from the given source and may be off by a few lines if the original file's blank-line layout differs.
limitations: The strip-method extent (4*(samples_per_pixel+1)*TIFFStripSize) cannot wrap while passing the quoted scanline/number_pixels gates and the rows_per_strip clamp — not exploitable.
The double-precision truncation of image->columns*samples_per_pixel*pow(2,...) is absorbed by the quoted 1.5*scanline check and the allocation NULL check.

chromaticity indexing and the colormap loop are guarded by quoted NULL checks and the quoted bits_per_sample/MaxColormapSize bound; sample_info[0..extra_samples-1] is consistent with the libtiff-owned count per callee contract.

A fully concrete (R,C) pair with 528*R*C mod 2^64 small was shown to exist by residue-class density (33 invertible mod 2^60, 128 representatives per residue, thousands of candidate extent values, offline search); exact pair not computed here.
